newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares edge up on local buying.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares edge up on local buying.

text.p: Leading Russian shares edged up on Friday on local buying, traders said.
At 0900 GMT the Russian Trading System index of 23 shares was 314.49 after closing at 314.07 on Thursday.
At 1000 GMT utility UES rose to $0.2175 from $0.2145 at Thursday's close, LUKoil edged up to $13.85 from $13.70 and Surgutneftegaz oil company was $0.825 after $0.793.
"Clear demand appeared at current levels," Regent European Securities trader Alexander Fonarkov said. "Demand from local participants is supporting the market at current levels."

East European Investment Co corporate securities head Nikolai Fomintsev forecast some operators who had pushed prices down on Thursday would close short positions today and would cause some price rise.
"I can suggest that either tonight or after the holidays we shall see some artificial growth," he said.
Russian markets are closed on Monday, March 10, for the International Women's Day holiday.
But he said the rise would be short-lived and prices would soon return to Friday's levels on profit-taking.
Traders said there was weak Western selling, but foreign operatos were not active.
"I saw Wastern sales, and maybe clients will sell more, but there will not be a storm of sales," Fonarkov said.
